title: Ὄνος καὶ τέττιγες
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 278. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », [ ] for words Chambry deletes as interpolated). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὄνος ἀκούσας τεττίγων ᾀδόντων [ἥσθη ἐπὶ τῇ εὐφωνίᾳ] καὶ ζηλώσας αὐτῶν τὴν εὐφωνίαν ἐπυνθάνετο τί σιτούμενοι τοιαύτην φωνὴν ἀφιᾶσι.
sentences.tr: Onos akousas tettigōn āidontōn [hēsthē epi tēi euphōniāi] kai zēlōsas autōn tēn euphōnian epynthaneto ti sitoumenoi toiautēn phōnēn aphiasi.
sentences.l: A donkey, having heard cicadas singing, [was delighted at the fine sound] and, having envied their fine voice, enquired what they were feeding on that they send forth such a voice.
sentences.i: A donkey heard cicadas singing [and took delight in the fine sound], and envying their fine voice he asked what they fed on to produce such a sound.
sentences.n: The square brackets are Chambry's mark for words he judges a later insertion and would delete — here a clause that says the donkey was pleased before the sentence goes on to say he was envious. He prints them so the seam stays visible, and the English keeps them. τί σιτούμενοι is an indirect question built on a circumstantial participle — 'feeding on what do they send forth such a voice?'

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ εἰπόντων· « Δρόσον, » ὁ ὄνος προσμένων δρόσον λιμῷ διεφθάρη.
sentences.tr: Tōn de eipontōn· « Droson, » ho onos prosmenōn droson limōi diephtharē.
sentences.l: And when they had said « Dew », the donkey, waiting for dew, was destroyed by hunger.
sentences.i: And when they said « Dew », the donkey held out for dew and perished of starvation.
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute, Τῶν δὲ εἰπόντων. λιμῷ is a dative of means. That the cicada lives on dew alone was the ordinary Greek belief about the insect, and the fable turns on it.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ οἱ τῶν παρὰ φύσιν ἐπιθυμοῦντες πρὸς τῷ μὴ ἐφικνεῖσθαι καὶ τὰ μέγιστα δυστυχοῦσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai hoi tōn para physin epithymountes pros tōi mē ephikneisthai kai ta megista dystychousin.
sentences.l: So too those who desire the things that are contrary to nature, besides not attaining them, are also unfortunate in the highest degree.
sentences.i: So too those who set their hearts on what is against nature not only fail of it but come to the worst of grief.
sentences.n: πρὸς τῷ … μὴ ἐφικνεῖσθαι is an articular infinitive after πρός with the dative, 'in addition to not attaining' — the same construction that closes fable 170, and the καί that follows is 'also'. ἐπιθυμέω takes the genitive of what is desired; τὰ μέγιστα is an adverbial accusative, 'in the greatest degree'.
